$$

The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic sine function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+1}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{arsinh}⁡4{x}^{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsinh}⁡4{x}^{6}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{{(4{x}^{6})}^{2}+1}}\cdot {(4{x}^{6})}^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{16{x}^{12}+1}}\cdot 24{x}^{5} \\  & =\frac{8{x}^{5}}{\sqrt{16{x}^{12}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$
